title: Spline curves gave no clear change in prior ozone by warmth slopes in four US bird samples in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether curved previous-season ozone and temperature responses changed their interaction with recorded bird richness. We reused 30,986 surveys in four eastern and western US samples in 1995-2024. The four-term spline estimates ranged from -0.491 to +0.208 recorded species per 10 ppb ozone and 2 C. All four corrected intervals included zero. No paired coefficient change was clear. The early western corrected interval was below zero with six spline terms, but included zero with four. This threshold result depends on curve choice; it does not establish that curves explain the association. Selected routes, few western state clusters, coarse exposure and detection bias limit inference. This is a model check on reused observations, not a causal climate test. Code, the verified input panel, source hashes, aggregate results and numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Original and spline interaction estimates use identical surveys and controls within each sample. Bars show four-test intervals. Added curves remove 2-24 percent of product variation left after original controls. This is shared model information, not richness explained.

citations.reason: We reuse its exact survey-augmented panel and numerical functions; biological observations fully overlap.
Earlier curve audit used current-season exposures and polynomial terms. We test previous-season exposures and splines.
Related trend decomposition used overlapping records; this study tests flexible main terms.
